title: fix: middleware refresh self-fetch hairpinned through the public domain
description: Middleware token refresh silently failed near-universally (~5min, not just long-idle) — every logged-in production user lost their session approximately every 5 minutes. middleware.ts's opportunistic refresh called fetch(new URL('/api/auth/refresh', request.url)) — a self-referential request using the incoming request's own URL as the fetch target. Behind the production reverse proxy (container bound to 127.0.0.1), request.url's protocol resolved as plain http; the self-fetch hit a 301 redirect to https, and fetch()'s default redirect:'follow' retried the redirect target as a GET (spec-mandated method downgrade on a 301 for a POST) — landing on this POST-only route as a silent 405. refreshRes.ok was false, so the cookie-refresh branch was skipped with no exception thrown, deterministically, every request.
design: Fix: the self-fetch now targets a fixed INTERNAL_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3000 (confirmed to match docker-compose.server.yml's published port and Next's standalone server.js listen port) instead of request.url — bypasses Cloudflare/Nginx/the public internet entirely for this one internal call, so there's no protocol to get wrong. Cookie forwarding and route.ts were confirmed correct and untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed live by reproducing the exact 301->GET->405 chain externally against production before the fix. Post-fix: repeated back-to-back real refreshes each produced a genuinely new saleor_token (iat incrementing each time). Re-ran the locale-bounce (front_store-rwq) and getInitialUser expiry (front_store-ipk) repros — no regression.
notes: Merged as fix/middleware-refresh-loopback, pending push/PR #50. executeGraphQL is confirmed unusable inside middleware (depends on next/headers cookies(), unavailable in middleware's execution context) — any future direct-GraphQL-in-middleware optimization must reuse route.ts's raw-fetch pattern instead. Deferred, not urgent since the loopback fix is sufficient on its own.
close_reason: Fixed and merged locally as fix/middleware-refresh-loopback (commit d1de684). Verified back-to-back real refreshes succeed with incrementing iat; no regression on front_store-rwq/front_store-ipk repros. Push/PR #50 still pending — reopen or track separately if that stalls.

title: Option d #1: zxf full fix - create transaction at Pay click and compare against live total before confirmPayment
description:
ORDER 1 of option (d) (ADR docs/adr/0001-checkout-v2-evaluation.md, patterns 1 + 3). Full fix for front_store-zxf.

SCOPE: stop creating the Stripe transaction when the Payment step mounts. Create it at the Pay click instead:
1. Mount Stripe Elements in deferred-intent mode (`mode: "payment"`, amount/currency from the page total, updated when the total changes) so the card form renders without a PaymentIntent.
2. On Pay: re-read the checkout from Saleor with its own query (not the page's `checkout` operation key - see front_store-auc), compare the displayed total with the live total, and if they differ block with a "your total changed" notice (no transactionInitialize).
3. Only then call transactionInitialize (optionally passing the live `amount`) and confirmPayment with the returned client secret; keep transactionProcess after confirm and the redirect-return reconciliation as today.
4. Apply the same displayed-vs-live compare to COD's Confirm (CODComponent already initializes at click).
proton_payments already creates the PaymentIntent for Saleor's authoritative total at TRANSACTION_INITIALIZE_SESSION (stripeWebhooks.ts:73-97), so init-at-click alone makes charge == Saleor total at click; the compare makes it == what the customer saw. Pattern 3 (lock totals-changing controls while paying) is already in place via PR #41; keep it.

FILES: src/checkout/sections/PaymentSection/StripeElements/stripeComponent.tsx, stripeElementsForm.tsx, types.ts; src/checkout/sections/PaymentSection/CODComponent/codComponent.tsx; src/checkout/sections/PaymentSection/PaymentMethods.tsx (if mount logic moves); src/checkout/lib/checkoutMessages.ts (price-change copy EN/AR). Reference: Paper execute-stripe-checkout-payment.ts:179-265, stripe-payment.tsx:33-47, actions.ts:504-519.

UNLOCK NEEDED: YES - PaymentSection/StripeElements/ (explicit approval). Live re-read may reuse CheckoutReadinessDocument from hooks/useCheckoutReadiness.ts read-only; if the hook itself must change, hooks/ unlock too. graphql/: not expected.

UNKNOWNS: deferred-intent Elements with our @stripe/stripe-js 2.2.0 / react-stripe-js 2.6.2 and with proton_payments' automatic_payment_methods PaymentIntents (cards likely; wallets untested).

VERIFY: zxf repro both directions (quantity/promo changed from another tab and from the cart page while Payment is open) -> price-change notice, no charge; Stripe guest + logged-in, 3DS redirect return, COD guest + logged-in; test-mode only, no production orders without explicit approval.

title: Stripe PaymentIntent amount is frozen at Payment-step mount: customer can be charged a different amount than the order total shown
description: MECHANISM: StripeComponent (src/checkout/sections/PaymentSection/StripeElements/stripeComponent.tsx) calls transactionInitialize once, in a useEffect keyed only on checkout.id, without an amount. proton-payments (com.tawasiplus.stripe_payment) creates the Stripe PaymentIntent for Saleor's checkout total AT THAT MOMENT. The order summary (quantity input, promo code) stays editable on the Payment step; changing it updates Saleor's total and the page display, but the Stripe component never re-initializes, so the PaymentIntent keeps the old amount and the Pay button stays enabled. COD is different: codComponent calls transactionInitialize at the Confirm click, so it uses Saleor's current total (correct vs Saleor, but can differ from a stale on-screen total). Adyen (not live) passes the page's own totalPrice explicitly - latent. EVIDENCE 2026-09-15 (production build of origin/main 689f1fc = the code live on tawasiplus.com, production API, Browser pane on screen 60fps; PaymentIntent amounts read from Stripe via stripe.retrievePaymentIntent, no payment confirmed, no orders): (1) UNDERCHARGE: checkout Q2hlY2tvdXQ6OTQzNGRmMWUtNGRlMy00NjdmLThiNjMtYTliYWQyZDBmMTRk, Payment step with card selected -> PI pi_3UG1dOQR8tmWIS1e06SHkRG2 = AED 13.99 = Saleor total; changed quantity 1->2 on the Payment step -> page 26.98, Saleor 26.98, same PI still 13.99, no new transactionInitialize. (2) OVERCHARGE: checkout Q2hlY2tvdXQ6NjFkNzBiNTAtZjk2Ny00YTk0LWE1OTMtZThiOTgxMTFkYmQ0 at qty 2 -> PI pi_3UG1lvQR8tmWIS1e0h51igOA = 26.98; quantity 2->1 -> page 13.99, Saleor 13.99, PI still 26.98, Pay button enabled. (3) STALE DISPLAY (scratch-only build that keeps last page data on a failed refetch, i.e. the state front_store-12e's fix would create): PI 13.99, quantity 1->2 with the page refetch failing -> page shows 13.99, Saleor 26.98, PI 13.99. COD under the same stale display (checkout Q2hlY2tvdXQ6NzE3OTM3MjAtNGRkNC00ZGU4LTg0MmEtMDhlODQ3NDY4MGU0): page 13.99, Confirm -> COD transaction charged 26.98 (chargeStatus FULL), checkoutComplete blocked so no order. Baseline COD (Q2hlY2tvdXQ6MDlmYWQ4NDItYzk0Mi00MTNjLTk3OWEtZTViN2E4NjA3ZmRi): quantity 1->2 then Confirm -> charged 26.98 = displayed = Saleor. NOT TESTED: what Saleor's checkoutComplete does after a real mismatched Stripe charge (needs a real test-mode charge; channel orderSettings.allowUnpaidOrders is staff-only). Expected per Saleor: undercharge -> chargeStatus PARTIAL -> CHECKOUT_NOT_FULLY_PAID after money was taken (unless unpaid orders allowed); overcharge -> OVERCHARGED, order completes, customer charged more than the order total. DO NOT OPEN the two COD test checkouts above: both have a FULL charge and the Payment step's usePayments would auto-complete them into orders. Fix direction (unverified): re-initialize the Stripe transaction whenever Saleor's total changes (or lock the summary on the Payment step / disable Pay until the PaymentIntent amount equals Saleor's current total), verified server-side rather than against page data. Touches StripeElements/ - needs explicit approval.

title: Checkout page swaps to not-found whenever any checkout query returns no data (e.g. a failed post-save refetch)
description:
views/Checkout/Checkout.tsx computes isCheckoutInvalid = !fetchingCheckout && !checkout && !isAuthenticating, treating 'the page checkout query currently has no data' as 'this checkout does not exist', and replaces the whole wizard with PageNotFound ('We couldn't fetch information about your checkout'). useCheckout() returns data?.checkout from urql's useCheckoutQuery, and urql replaces the operation's state with each result, so ANY error result on that operation key (network failure, HTTP 5xx, GraphQL error with data:null) makes checkout undefined. The page query is re-executed network-only by urql's document cacheExchange after every mutation (every autosave/commit), so a single transient failure of that refetch throws a customer with a perfectly valid cart onto the not-found page; only a reload recovers.

OBSERVED 2026-09-14 (production build of fix/readiness-cache-key-auc vs https://api.tawasiplus.com/graphql/, guest checkout Q2hlY2tvdXQ6N2QwNjQyMjQtNDYzNC00M2E0LTg2ZGQtZjhjMDg4ZDU5ODBh): on the Shipping step changed street to 'Refetch Fail Street 13'; checkoutShippingAddressUpdate returned 200 and Saleor holds the new address, then the automatic post-save 'checkout' refetch was failed with an injected network error -> PageNotFound within ~1s. Side effect: the follow-on billing mirror save never ran (its form unmounted), so billing stayed on the old street. front_store-auc removed one trigger (the readiness check shared this key); this is the remaining class.

Fix direction (unverified): keep the last good checkout when a refetch errors (only treat checkout(id:) === null from a successful response as 'does not exist'), show a non-destructive retry/offline notice instead of PageNotFound, and consider retrying transient refetch failures. Checkout.tsx is under src/checkout/views - needs explicit approval per CLAUDE.md rules.
notes:
2026-09-15: charge-amount investigation found a separate P0, filed as front_store-zxf (Stripe PaymentIntent frozen at Payment-step mount; COD charges Saleor's total at click, so a stale display can differ from both). Implementation of 12e paused pending user review. Ripple-check conclusion for the planned 'keep last good data' change: stale page data must never be allowed to drive a payment action - while the page checkout query is in its error state the Payment step's Pay/Confirm must be blocked (not unmounted mid-payment), in addition to blocking Continue; the readiness check (own query) stays the backstop for delivery method/address skips that stale shouldAbort comparisons could cause. Test checkouts created: Q2hlY2tvdXQ6OTQzNGRmMWUtNGRlMy00NjdmLThiNjMtYTliYWQyZDBmMTRk, Q2hlY2tvdXQ6NGE5NDBjZDgtYzAwZi00M2M3LWFiYTctZDlmZTc5MTAwNmVi, Q2hlY2tvdXQ6NjFkNzBiNTAtZjk2Ny00YTk0LWE1OTMtZThiOTgxMTFkYmQ0 (Stripe PIs never confirmed); DO NOT OPEN (FULL COD charge, would auto-complete into orders): Q2hlY2tvdXQ6MDlmYWQ4NDItYzk0Mi00MTNjLTk3OWEtZTViN2E4NjA3ZmRi, Q2hlY2tvdXQ6NzE3OTM3MjAtNGRkNC00ZGU4LTg0MmEtMDhlODQ3NDY4MGU0.
2026-09-16 OPTION (d) DECISION (docs/adr/0001-checkout-v2-evaluation.md): 12e is item #4 of epic front_store-frm (ADR pattern 4: keep last good checkout on a failed refresh; only a SUCCESSFUL response with checkout(id:) === null means "does not exist"; model error vs not_found as separate states, like Paper's loadState). Option (d) CHANGES the approved design; it does not replace it.
KEPT: keep-last-good page data instead of PageNotFound on an error result; retry the page query 3x at 1s/2s/4s then every ~10s in the background; approved EN/AR connection banner + Try again; Continue blocked while stale; log prefix/source distinct from [checkout-readiness:fail-open].
CHANGED: (1) "Block Pay/Confirm (cover, don't unmount) while page data is stale" is no longer part of 12e - it is superseded by front_store-frm.1, whose Pay/Confirm-click live re-read + displayed-vs-live compare blocks any payment on a stale total regardless of page state. 12e therefore depends on frm.1 and must not ship before it. (2) The billing-mismatch notice with "Use my shipping address" is kept only as an INTERIM guard for the lost follow-on billing write; front_store-frm.4 (explicit commits, billing written once at Pay, no effect-driven billing mirror) removes that failure mode, and the notice should be re-evaluated/removed there.

Checkout.tsx only shows PageNotFound when the server authoritatively confirms absence; an error with prior data shows the page normally plus a retry banner, an error with no prior data shows a distinct load-failed screen (not not-found wording). comments.author: Ibraim
comments.text:
PARKED 2026-09-15: blocked pending the Saleor Paper checkout v2 evaluation. No part of 12e implemented; branch fix/checkout-refetch-failure-12e holds no code changes.

RIPPLE ANALYSIS: what changes if useCheckout() returns last-good (stale) data plus an error state instead of nothing. Evidence base: production build vs production API, pane on screen, 2026-09-14/15; see earlier notes and front_store-zxf.

Consumers where stale data changes BEHAVIOUR (not only display):
- Payment amount (CODComponent, StripeComponent). Neither passes an amount to transactionInitialize, so Saleor computes it server-side and stale page data cannot change what is charged. It can, however, let the customer confirm against a total they never saw. Proven with a scratch build that keeps stale data: page 13.99, COD charged Saleor's 26.98. Consequence: Pay/Confirm must be blocked while page data is stale, not only Continue. Block by covering the payment area, never by unmounting it, which could kill Stripe reconciliation mid-payment.
- usePaymentGatewaysInitialize: re-initializes gateways only when the page's billing country changes, so a billing-country change is missed while stale. Covered by the payment block above.
- usePayments: a stale chargeStatus only delays its auto-complete; completionFailed still reports errors. No wrong action.
- useDeliveryMethodsForm: shouldAbort (selectedMethodId === checkout.deliveryMethod?.id) and the commit's "already saved" check compare against page data, so stale data can SILENTLY SKIP a needed delivery-method write. Only backstop: the readiness check, which reads Saleor with its own query and blocks with "Please choose a delivery method."
- Address and email commits (useAutoSaveAddressForm savedAddress, useCheckoutEmailUpdate checkout.email, address-list forms): "skip if unchanged" comparisons use the page copy. Stale data causes a redundant write or, rarely, a skipped one; the readiness check catches a missing field.
- useBillingSameAsShippingForm: with stale data it waits rather than writing a wrong address (diagnostic E2). The mismatch notice (fix 4) must compare FRESH data or it will raise false notices.
- useCustomerAttach: stale user may re-attempt the attach; the "already attached" error already triggers a refetch. Harmless.
- Summary quantity / promo code (useSummaryItemForm, SummaryPromoCodeRow): use the page's line IDs and state. A stale ID gives a visible API error, not a silent wrong write. Stale totals are the zxf display problem.
- CheckoutForm GA4 events: analytics values only.
- Readiness check: its own query, unaffected. It remains the backstop.

THREE OPEN DECISIONS (as asked, with the user's rulings 2026-09-15):
1. Order of work: fix zxf first (needs StripeElements/ approval) or 12e first with a payment block. RULING: StripeElements/ stays off limits; a UI-only zxf mitigation was proposed separately. 12e parked.
2. Real test-mode charge to confirm Saleor's under/overcharge behaviour. RULING: NO. No orders on production.
3. Block Pay/Confirm in CheckoutForm.tsx (cover, don't unmount) while page data is stale. RULING: deferred with 12e.

Approved-but-unimplemented design elements, kept for whoever resumes:
- Retry the page query 3x at 1s/2s/4s, then keep retrying every ~10s in the background so the page self-heals with no click.
- Banner copy approved: EN "We're having trouble connecting. We'll keep trying — please stay on this page." [Try again]; AR «تعذّر الاتصال بالخادم. نحاول إعادة الاتصال — يرجى البقاء في هذه الصفحة.» [إعادة المحاولة].
- Mismatch notice approved with an action button: "Use my shipping address" / «استخدام عنوان الشحن»; billing and shipping shown on separate lines.
- Continue blocked while stale; logged with a prefix/source distinct from [checkout-readiness:fail-open].

title: [bug] /login and /register 500 — Server Component passes function prop to Client Component
description: Both (main)/login/page.tsx and (main)/register/page.tsx are async Server Components (call cookies()/redirect()/getTranslations) that render <AuthFormWrapper mode="login" onModeChange={() => undefined} />. AuthFormWrapper.tsx is a Client Component ("use client"). Passing an inline arrow function as a prop from a Server Component to a Client Component is invalid under Next.js 15's RSC model and throws server-side on every request: 'Error: Event handlers cannot be passed to Client Component props ... digest: 3534376298'. Confirmed live in session 34 (account-deletion work) via a fresh next dev run with .next cache fully cleared, so this is not stale-build noise -- it reproduces from a clean build. Net effect: every visit to /login or /register currently 500s for any visitor, on both locales. This directly matches unverified checklist item 9 in front_store-u40 (Verify auth flow end-to-end), which has been open and unclaimed since session 8 -- this bug likely existed undetected the whole time. Fix: make AuthFormWrapper's onModeChange prop optional with an internal no-op default, and drop the onModeChange={() => undefined} passed from both standalone pages (AuthModal.tsx's own usage, which passes setAuthModalMode client-to-client, is fine and must not be touched).
acceptance_criteria: Fresh next dev + cleared .next: /en/uae-channel/login and /en/uae-channel/register both render the form with zero console/server errors, in both en and ar. pnpm tsc --noEmit clean, pnpm lint at baseline (<=7 warnings, all pre-existing in src/checkout/ + Logo.tsx).
close_reason: Fixed on hotfix/login-register-rsc-crash: AuthFormWrapper's onModeChange made optional with a no-op default; both standalone pages' inline onModeChange={() => undefined} removed. Verified live: /en+/ar /login and /register both render with zero console/server errors on a fresh next dev + cleared .next. tsc clean, lint at baseline.

title: fix: getInitialUser() had no JWT expiry check
description: getInitialUser() in [locale]/[channel]/layout.tsx (which seeds AuthContext's initialUser) decoded the saleor_token cookie's JWT payload with no exp check at all — any syntactically-valid, present cookie was trusted as 'logged in' regardless of whether it had actually expired. Confirmed deterministic via a fresh, uncached SSR of /login with an expired-but-decodable cookie: rendered both the login form (correct) and the UserMenu with the stale email (wrong) in the same response.
design: Fix: getInitialUser() now checks isExpired(token) — a new export in src/lib/auth/jwt.ts, a thin wrapper around the existing isTokenExpiringSoon(token, 0) — and returns null for an expired token, same as the missing-token branch. Deliberately kept as a cheap local check, not a resolveAuthenticatedUser()-style network call, since this layout wraps nearly every route in the app.
acceptance_criteria: Live-verified: expired-cookie repro now renders the header logged-out (no stale email, no UserMenu marker); a genuinely-valid session still renders logged-in normally.
notes: Merged via PR #49. Surfaced as a follow-up diagnostic on front_store-rwq.
close_reason: Merged via PR #49 — verified expired-cookie repro shows logged-out header, valid sessions unaffected.

title: fix: idle-session bounce through /login dropped locale/channel prefix
description: After an idle session (expired access token + failed/expired refresh), navigating to /account bounced through /login and then to a bare, locale-less '/', which next-intl renegotiated via Accept-Language — landing Arabic-preferring browsers on the Arabic homepage instead of back on /account. Two chained bugs: (1) login/register/reset-password pages guarded themselves with a bare cookie-presence check instead of validating the token; (2) that branch's target, bare redirect('/'), has no locale/channel segment, and next-intl's NEXT_LOCALE cookie is session-only (no Max-Age), so a browser restart drops it and negotiation falls through to Accept-Language.

title: Readiness check fail-open broken for network/HTTP/GraphQL errors: failed urql re-read replaces checkout view with not-found
description: Found while verifying the fail-open observability record (Phase 2 pre-push verification). useCheckoutReadiness re-reads the checkout with client.query(CheckoutDocument, same variables, network-only), which shares its urql operation key with every mounted useCheckout(). When that request fails with a network error (reproduced by rejecting the readiness fetch in a production build against the production API), urql publishes the error result under the shared key: useCheckout()'s data becomes undefined, so views/Checkout/Checkout.tsx renders PageNotFound ('We couldn't fetch information about your checkout') instead of the wizard advancing. goNext did fail open and logged [checkout-readiness:fail-open] {reason: network, attempts: 1, elapsedMs: 1, source: step-advance}, but the page is gone; a reload recovers (checkout intact). Expected to apply equally to HTTP and GraphQL errors (error result without data); timeouts DO fail open correctly (verified: step-advance record at 8.0s, advance at 8.4s; payment-guard record, gateways at 17.1s; a hung request also dedupes both checks onto one in-flight key). Behaviour dates from Phase 1 (live via PR #38), not introduced by Phase 2. Direction (unverified): read through a request that does not share the useCheckout operation key (e.g. a distinct document/variables or a plain fetch with deduplicated fragments - see the discarded hotfix: raw print of CheckoutDocument duplicates the Money fragment and Saleor returns 400), so a failed check cannot overwrite the page's checkout data.
notes: FIX COMMITTED LOCALLY on fix/readiness-cache-key-auc (not pushed). Mechanism confirmed (urql one result stream per operation key; readiness shared useCheckout's key; error result -> page data undefined -> PageNotFound, and CheckoutForm unmount made verify() return cancelled so the step check never logged). Fix: CheckoutReadinessDocument (CheckoutDocument AST, operation renamed), subscribe+unsubscribe on timeout (a timed-out toPromise left the op active and later same-key checks piggybacked on the dead request), one shared 8s budget per Continue click (commits raced -> verifyFailed; step check; Payment guard reuses the deadline). Guest verification complete on production build vs production API (see CLAUDE.md). KEEP OPEN: logged-in runs (normal, rushed, 3 error classes, stale-state compare) still pending - need a signed-in session in the test browser. Separate class filed as front_store-12e.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/readiness-cache-key-auc (commit 48dbf31 + docs follow-up). MECHANISM (confirmed in @urql/core 4.3.0 source and reproduced on a production build vs the production API for network, HTTP 502 and GraphQL errors): urql's operation key = hash(document text + operation name) + variables, and the client shares one result stream per key (results are filtered by key only). The readiness re-read used CheckoutDocument with useCheckout()'s variables, so its error result was delivered to the page's useCheckout(): data became undefined, Checkout.tsx rendered PageNotFound, and CheckoutForm unmounted before verify() resumed, so it returned 'cancelled' and the step check never logged a fail-open record. FIX: CheckoutReadinessDocument (CheckoutDocument's AST definitions, operation renamed; new {kind, definitions} object so loc/__key aren't carried over); subscribe + unsubscribe on timeout (a timed-out toPromise() left the operation active and later same-key checks piggybacked on the dead request); one 8s budget per Continue click shared by commits, the step check and the Payment guard. VERIFIED guest and logged-in: all three error classes fail open from the step check (source step-advance) and the guard (source payment-guard) with the correct reason, no not-found; normal and rushed advances keep the page's checkout current (total, shipping price, delivery method, quantities, both addresses equal a fresh Saleor read); no extra checkout queries. Real on-screen hung-network worst case: spinner/timeout record 8.0s, Payment step 8.3s, payment methods 9.25s (was ~17s). Remaining class filed as front_store-12e (P0).

title: Debounced checkout field updates (delivery method, email, address) can be silently lost if customer advances quickly
description:
Discovered during Session 49's checkoutComplete retry-loop investigation (front_store, see CLAUDE.md Known Issues + Checkout Sub-App section).

useDebouncedSubmit (src/checkout/hooks/useDebouncedSubmit.ts) debounces field-update mutations by 2 seconds. The Shipping/Contact step's component tree fully unmounts the moment the wizard advances (AnimatePresence + key={currentStep} in CheckoutForm.tsx), which triggers useDebouncedSubmit's cleanup effect and CANCELS any still-pending debounced call outright -- not defers it, cancels it.

This means a customer who moves through Contact or Shipping faster than ~2 seconds (very achievable -- Aramex is pre-selected by default, so a fast customer might just click through without any pause) can reach Payment with that field NEVER PERSISTED server-side, even though the UI showed it as filled/selected the whole time. Confirmed live in production via a genuine UI walkthrough (no GraphQL shortcuts): reached a real checkout with chargeStatus:FULL (COD's transactionInitialize succeeds unconditionally, doesn't check this) and email:null.

This affects at least three forms sharing the same useDebouncedSubmit pattern:
- useDeliveryMethodsForm.ts (delivery method)
- useCheckoutEmailUpdate.ts (email)
- useAddressListForm.ts (address)

Session 49 fixed the SYMPTOM (usePayments.ts's infinite checkoutComplete retry loop that resulted from this), but deliberately did not fix this underlying race -- out of that fix's scope. Fields can still silently fail to persist; they just no longer cause a runaway retry loop when checkoutComplete then rejects the (now correctly failing, gracefully surfaced) completion attempt.

Possible directions for a future fix (not decided, needs its own investigation): flush the debounced submit on unmount instead of canceling it (debounce.flush() before cancel in the cleanup effect), or block wizard advancement until the pending mutation resolves, or increase the debounce window's safety margin. title: Stripe checkout: transactionProcess never fires, null.id TypeError in stripeElementsForm.tsx
description:
During the Session 47 'Final Combined Fix' test loop (redirect-aware gateway selection + safety-net token), discovered that the primary Stripe reconciliation path never actually works: transactionProcess is never called successfully client-side.

Reproduced across 3 separate real test orders (#28 non-redirect, #29 forced 3DS redirect via test card 4000002500003155, #30 non-redirect clean-signal test) on production (tawasiplus.com) after both this session's fixes were deployed:
- Saleor's own webhook-dispatch debug log shows ZERO 'Sending payload...for event transaction_process_session' lines, despite the app's Webhook row (id 106, com.tawasiplus.stripe_payment) being correctly subscribed to that event (confirmed via Django shell).
- proton-payments' own request log likewise shows zero transaction_process_session hits.
- Browser console (read_console_messages, captured right after clicking Pay on order #30) showed a repeated client-side error immediately after payment submission: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading id)', originating from the Stripe checkout bundle chunks (4718-f447e6003ff46ae7.js and 7cf2dd7c-2503145de182659a.js).

Root cause hypothesis (not yet fixed, not yet fully isolated): something in stripeElementsForm.tsx's post-confirmPayment flow reads .id off a value that's null (likely the transaction id sourced from getUrlForTransactionInitialize() or the URL's transaction param) before calling transactionProcess({id: transactionId}) — throwing before the GraphQL request is ever sent, which is consistent with Saleor never seeing an incoming mutation at all.

Impact: every Stripe order on production is currently being completed ONLY via the async Stripe-webhook safety net (reportTransactionEvent, Session 47's Fix 2), not via the synchronous transactionProcess path the code is designed around. This works today because Stripe's own webhook is reliable, but it means there is no redundancy left \u2014 if Stripe's webhook were ever delayed or failed, a customer would be stuck on the 'Almost done...' overlay indefinitely despite Fix 1 (redirect-aware gateway selection) correctly getting them back to the Payment step.

This file (src/checkout/sections/PaymentSection/StripeElements/stripeElementsForm.tsx) is on this project's do-not-touch-without-explicit-approval list, so it was left unmodified. User explicitly chose to file this rather than fix it in Session 47.

All 3 real Stripe test PaymentIntents from this diagnosis were refunded and all 4 test orders (#28-#31) canceled during Session 47's cleanup.
notes:
RESOLVED (Session 48). Root cause precisely identified: src/checkout/hooks/useCheckoutComplete.ts line 9 destructured checkout.id from useCheckout() with no null guard. useCheckout() legitimately returns checkout:null once a checkout has been converted into an Order (a real state, not hypothetical) -- Stripe's async webhook safety net (Session 47 Fix 2) can finish that conversion before the browser's own confirmPayment()->transactionProcess->onCheckoutComplete() chain gets back around to a render. useCheckoutComplete is called unconditionally by every payment method (Stripe, Adyen, COD, DummyDropIn), so the crash was reachable from all of them, though only Stripe's async-safety-net race made it likely in practice.

Fix: guarded the destructure (checkout?.id), and added an explicit guard in the returned onCheckoutComplete callback that short-circuits with a graceful payment.unexpectedError toast instead of ever calling submit() when checkoutId is absent -- necessary because useSubmit()'s own internal handleSubmit ALSO reads checkout.id/checkout.channel.slug unconditionally (same latent bug, one level down, in a hook outside this session's approval scope) and would have thrown the identical crash if reached with a null checkout.

Item 4 (red 'duplicate/failed' banner on OrderConfirmation): searched the entire codebase, found no UI string matching that description. Believe it is the user's description of the existing payment.unexpectedError toast (confirmed real, and displayed by the exact code path this fix now guards) rather than a second, separate bug -- could not confirm with certainty against the actual customer-facing screen.

Verified live (local dev pointed at production Saleor/proton-payments, since this session's instructions were commit-only-do-not-push): order #34 -- checkout genuinely transitioned to null mid-flow (confirmed via checkout(id) query returning null immediately after), onCheckoutComplete completed cleanly with zero errors, chargeStatus FULL, no crash. This is the exact race the bug depended on, occurring naturally without needing a forced redirect delay.

transaction_process_session webhook still does not appear in proton-payments' logs even post-fix -- re-analyzed and this is now understood to be EXPECTED Saleor behavor (the resolver skips re-invoking the app webhook when the transaction is already resolved via the async safety net), not a bug. The client's own transactionProcess mutation call does succeed and drives checkoutComplete correctly, evidenced by order 34 completing via the primary path with no crash.

tsc clean, lint clean (6 pre-existing warnings, none new). Only src/checkout/hooks/useCheckoutComplete.ts changed (git diff --name-only confirmed). Committed locally, not pushed per explicit instruction (payment-critical, awaiting review).
close_reason: Fixed in Session 48: guarded checkout.id destructure in useCheckoutComplete.ts + onCheckoutComplete guard. See issue notes for full root cause and verification.

title: Checkout customer recognition — logged-in users treated as guests
description: Logged-in customers (valid saleor_token cookie) were treated as guests at /checkout — shown the register/login prompt, saved addresses never offered. Guests and every other route are unaffected; the cookie is never set when saleor_token is absent.

title: Refresh threshold exactly equals access-token TTL — wasteful refresh on nearly every request
description: src/lib/auth/jwt.ts's isTokenExpiringSoon() defaults thresholdSeconds to 300, and Saleor's default JWT_TTL_ACCESS is also 300s (5 minutes, confirmed measured directly against production, not assumed). Since the threshold equals the TTL, the access token is 'expiring soon' from essentially the moment it's minted, so middleware.ts's opportunistic refresh fires on nearly every single request for the whole time a user is logged in — not just as the token nears real expiry. Discovered as a contributing factor while diagnosing front_store-aa0 (the middleware self-fetch hairpin bug): every request re-attempting a refresh is what made that bug's impact 'near-universal' rather than occasional.
design: Works correctly now that front_store-aa0 is fixed, but is wasteful — an extra internal loopback fetch + Saleor GraphQL round-trip on effectively every navigation while logged in. Consider either widening the gap between the threshold and the TTL (e.g. lower the threshold to something like 60-90s so refresh only fires when actually close to expiry) or widening JWT_TTL_ACCESS itself server-side. Either needs to preserve the existing 'refresh happens well before real expiry' safety margin.
acceptance_criteria: A logged-in session's steady-state navigation no longer triggers a refresh attempt on every single request; refresh still reliably occurs before the access token actually expires.

value: urql (@urql/core 4.x) gotchas for src/checkout: (1) operation key = hash(document text + operation name) + variables and the client shares ONE result stream per key, so any query with the same document+variables as a mounted useQuery (e.g. useCheckout) delivers its error result into that hook's state; give side reads their own operation name (build a new {kind, definitions} object from the generated AST - never spread, spreading copies loc and urql's cached __key and keeps the old key). (2) Promise.race(timeout, source.toPromise()) never tears the operation down: a hung op stays active and later same-key queries dedupe onto it without sending a request - subscribe and unsubscribe on timeout instead. (3) Browser-test harness: when this session is not open in any window the Browser pane throttles requestAnimationFrame to ~0-6fps even though visibilityState says visible; interleave computer screenshots during waits to keep framer-motion step transitions progressing.

Claude Browser pane gotcha: when the in-app Browser pane is HIDDEN, document.visibilityState is 'hidden' and requestAnimationFrame never fires (timers and fetch still run). The checkout wizard's framer-motion AnimatePresence mode='wait' step transition then never finishes, so the UI freezes on the previous step's last frame (e.g. a stuck 'Checking your details...' button) and looks exactly like a hang. This caused a false production-outage alarm and an unnecessary rollback/hotfix during Phase 1 (front_store-0ev). Before trusting any UI timing/hang observation, assert document.visibilityState==='visible' and that a requestAnimationFrame callback fires (take a screenshot to make the pane render).
